pr_title: Ignore order of SQL joins, select, includes, left_outer_joins, eager_load and preload for ActiveRecord::Relation#or & for ActiveRecord::Relation#and
pr_body:
### Summary

Fixes https://github.com/rails/rails/issues/45398

Ignore order of SQL joins, select, includes, left_outer_joins, eager_load and preload for ActiveRecord::Relation#or & for ActiveRecord::Relation#and
pr_comments: I haven't taken the time to actually invent examples, but my recollection is that ordering of left joins can affect the query results (at least, I have strong memories that the PostgreSQL optimizer is more limited in how it can reorder a LEFT JOIN-using query plan over an otherwise equivalent JOIN version). @sampatbadhe  are you certain this is safe?

issue_context.title: Order of SQL JOINs should not matter for ActiveRecord::Relation#or
issue_context.body:
### Steps to reproduce

Consider we have some model with associations.

```ruby
class User < ApplicationRecord
  has_many :posts
  has_many :comments
end
```

Then we want to use `ActiveRecord::Relation#or` to build some query.

```ruby
  User.joins(:posts, :comments).where(comments: { id: 1 }).or(User.joins(:comments, :posts).where(posts: { id: 2 }))
```

### Expected behavior

It should produce a valid SQL query with two JOINs (final order of JOIN statements can be determined from one of subqueries).

```ruby
User.joins(:posts, :comments).where(comments: { id: 1 }).or(User.joins(:comments, :posts).where(posts: { id: 2 }))

# SELECT "users".* FROM "users" INNER JOIN "posts" ON "posts"."user_id" = "users"."id" INNER JOIN "comments" ON "comments"."user_id" = "users"."id" WHERE ("comments"."id" = $1 OR "posts"."id" = $2)  [["id", 1], ["id", 2]]
```

### Actual behavior

But it raises an error due to arguments order difference in #joins.

```ruby
User.joins(:posts, :comments).where(comments: { id: 1 }).or(User.joins(:comments, :posts).where(posts: { id: 2 }))

# Relation passed to #or must be structurally compatible. Incompatible values: [:joins] (ArgumentError)
```

### Notes

This problem exists for all methods provided in `STRUCTURAL_VALUE_METHODS` constant in `ActiveRecord::QueryMethods`. I think for most of them arguments order should not be checked.

### System configuration
**Rails version**: 7.0.3

**Ruby version**: 3.1.2

review_comments: This assertion is asserting the whole block rather than each of these calls. Asserting that nothing is raised doesn't tell us much about what our expectations are. These assertions should instead assert the return values for each call. If something is raised then the test will fail.

This name doesn't make sense to me. It says "to ignore order" but then we sort below, essentially the opposite of ignoring order because we set an explicit order. I think this needs a better (and shorter) name.

Also in your issue it said "This problem exists for all methods provided in STRUCTURAL_VALUE_METHODS constant in ActiveRecord::QueryMethods. I think for most of them arguments order should not be checked." but this isn't most of the methods in STRUCTURAL_VALUE_METHODS, so are we missing some? or was that assertion incorrect?
